title: MVQ: Towards Efficient DNN Compression and Acceleration with Masked Vector Quantization
problem: Conventional vector quantization (VQ) for DNN compression treats all weights equally during k-means clustering, forcing important high-magnitude weights to align with unimportant zero-adjacent weights, causing large clustering errors on the weights that most affect accuracy and leading to significant accuracy degradation at high compression ratios.
motivation: Edge DNN deployment requires extreme compression ratios (20-30x) to fit models on-chip, but standard VQ methods sacrifice too much accuracy at these ratios because they fail to protect the important weights that govern model behavior.
method: MVQ combines two complementary techniques. At the algorithm level, it removes unimportant weights using N:M structured pruning (eliminating weights in a regular, predictable pattern), then applies masked k-means clustering—which groups only important weights and ignores pruned zeros so they don't distort the cluster centers—converts to 8-bit symmetric quantization of the codebook, and refines accuracy by updating only unpruned weights during finetuning. At the hardware level, a specialized accelerator using Enhanced Weight Stationary dataflow reconstructs sparse weights dynamically from the codebook and N:M mask using a Codebook Register File and LZC-based mask decoder, and employs a systolic array (grid of processing elements) with Q=N/M × d active elements per subvector instead of the full d, reducing multiplier and register file count by 55%. The design was synthesized at 40nm using 0.99V low-threshold transistors with Synopsys Design Compiler.
key_novelty: Masked k-means clustering that only includes important, unpruned weights when assigning to clusters and updating their centers, preventing pruned zeros from distorting the averages so the codebook stays close to the weights that matter for accuracy.
contributions: Empirical demonstration that clustering error on important weights (not total SSE) is the key driver of VQ accuracy loss
Masked k-means algorithm excluding pruned weights from distance computation and centroid updates
Sparsity-aware EWS systolic array with Q active PEs per tile reducing array size by 55%
Assignment-aware weight-loading controller with CRF and LZC-based N:M mask decoder

metrics.speedup: EWS-CMS achieves 1.2-2.2x speedup over EWS baseline on 64x64 array
metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 2.3x energy efficiency improvement vs base EWS accelerator; 1.73x vs prior sparse accelerators; 6.9 TOPS/W for ResNet-18 64x64 at 40nm; 53.3-137.9% higher efficiency vs EWS baseline
metrics.area: 55% reduction in systolic array size vs EWS baseline at 75% sparsity
metrics.ppa: 40nm 0.99V; 73% higher energy efficiency vs S2TA (normalized to 40nm)
metrics.accuracy: ResNet-18: 68.8% top-1 at ~22x compression (vs 68.2% PQF, 66.5% BGD); ResNet-50: 75.2% at ~22x (vs 74.2% PQF); VGG-16: 69.7% at ~28x; reduces FLOPs by ~70% (50% for lightweight models)
metrics.other: Evaluated on ResNet-18/50, VGG-16, AlexNet, MobileNet-v1/v2, EfficientNet, MaskRCNN/COCO, DeepLab-V3/VOC

limitations: Depthwise convolution layers do not benefit from MVQ because the small parameter count means weight loading is not the bottleneck; only pointwise convolution results reported for lightweight models.
primary_theme: masked vector quantization with sparsity-aware systolic array for CNN compression
